title: <input> type values little use
body:
type="password" is handy for concealing the text of a password -- even if it's advisable to to have a Show/Hide button next to it.

But what about the other types ?

    type="email" does not use the standard regex for an email address, let alone special regexs for Gmail and other mail types. As far as I can see it just forbids any of the characters ()£%@\<> in the address handle. It does nothing to ensure a period character is present in the domain name. When a period is present in the domain name, it is not allowed as its first or last character. And the period need only be followed by ONE letter or digit -- not two.

    type="tel" is worse than useless. It doesn't even check the characters to ensure they are all (or bar an opening '+') numeric. Would it be that hard to subdivide this field into 3 sub-fields representing international, area and local numbers ? Coders could then populate these as they wish for their web app and compose their own validations.

    type="color" works on Firefox and Chrome but need a bit of restyling.

    type="date" does not work on Firefox - anything goes. In Chrome it functions but with a crude appearance and none of the usual checks for days in the month, leap years and plausible year range.

    type="datetime" won't work on Firefox or Chrome.

    type="datetime-local" only runs - crudely - on Chrome.

    type="month" only runs on Chrome.

    type="number" does what it should for (un)signed int and real numbers.

    type="range" produces a nice slider in Chrome and Firefox but without max, min and current values displayed.

    type="search" does nothing on Firefox or Chrome.

    type="time" does nothing on Firefox but shows a 24-hour hh:mm:ss display on Chrome. Illegal time entry overwritten by a more plausible one.

    type="url" half-works on both Firefox and Chrome. Sometimes it validates correctly, sometimes not.

    type="week" works on Chrome, not on Firefox.

These are all the attributes I know of. But it seems that browser coders have come to the conclusion that these descriptors are not usually worthwhile to implement.

Most disappointing is the absence of adequate definition and validation for the email, password and tel types.
I believe improvements are needed here.
